[LCS] Analysis & Perspective - Week 8 Picks & Bans

Hello Voat ! Today I'm gonna talk about the picks and bans phase of week 8, in the EU LCS. At first, I wrote an heavy stats-loaded article but it had so many irrelevant numbers that I decided to go with a different approach. We'll focus on the contested picks and I'll try to give a perspective (my perspective, and I'm waiting for yours) on why these picks are so contested. In the week 8, 43 champions were played. Yet, 6 of these champs were seens in 80% or more of the games : Rek'Sai - Ryze - Sivir - Corki - Rumble - Shen. Let's take look on these champions !

 

1 - Rek'Sai - 3W 4L - 3 Bans

Queen of the jungle, the true one. The main strength of our girly monster is simply her lack of downside. You could nerf her to hell, her kit simply makes her so strong, she reminds my a bit of Thresh. Early/mid/late game, she doesn't care, she is strong all the game long. Great mobility, good sustain, fast clear camp, a global presence and a damn good ganker. Moreover, she offers a ton of vision-based utility ; in other words, a good Rek'Sai controls not only the jungle or the lanes, but the pace of the game. Like Evelynn, she will force the enemy team to act as a team and react together if they don't want to be eaten by Rek'Sai. She's the most contested jungler as she offers so much and fits in any composition. Yet, despite that, she's barely around 40% win this week. Pros know how to play against a Rek'Sai and, furthermore, other junglers have been rising. All-around speaking, she is unmatched. But you're looking for a role player, you'll chose someone else : Nunu offers more peel and can transform your Azir in a dreadful beast, Gragas has no rival when it comes to space and crowd control, and Nidalee offers an excellent early-assassination potential mixed with tons of utilty. Don't take it wrong, Rek'Sai is the true queen of the jungle, but I bet her reign is slowly coming to an end.

 

2 - Ryze - 1L - 9 Bans

To be honest, I haven't got much insight on why he's such a contested pick. I believe it's for the pressure a Ryze puts on the early game. Let me explain : Ryze is such a late game threat, you wanna shut it down when he's still weak. Picking Ryze forces the enemy team to a laneswap and allows you to chose where to set your double lane. Furthermore, Ryze is a jungler-magnet. He will be ganked, dived, spanked and spitted on. Put your Ryze on the toplane and the enemy has to virtually concede the first drakes and the bot tower. Ryze is far from being a "I WIN"-button but he's so annoying to face. I could still go a long way explaining why picking Ryze alters the early game strategy but I think you've got it already. However, we must highlight that picking Ryze is risky. It's a losing lane and your team will be 4vs5 on the midgame, not to mention that he can feed the enemy Rek'Sai/Nidalee/Kalista/Corki, putting your team in a difficult situation. I've always found that backlash not worth the risk but we can't ignore his impact on a game. Either you ban him or prepare yourself to invest a lot to shut him down.

 

3 - Sivir - 10 Bans

Ah, 100% banned. Kassadin would be proud of you, Sivir. So, why is that ? To set it simply : Sivir is scary. And not in a good way. In the current meta, poke comps are god tier. The damage output combined with a lack of midlane assassins and play-a-tank-top makes the double-ad-comp or, with the recent item changes, Ez/Kog/Azir mid so damn good. Basically, you need two things for a composition like that : at least one low-cooldown long-range damage dealer (Jayce, Varus, Ezreal, Kogmaw, etc.) and a way to prevent being all-in, aka a disengage. Sivir offers you a poke tool, one of the best waveclear among adc's, a safe lanephase thanks to her shield and a team speed boost. In other words, she, alone, can counter a poke team or, worst, make a poke team virtually untouchable. Among all champs, she's by far the most contested pick because she's the most powerful available tool you can get during teambuilding. We saw it yestarday in the CLG - C9 game : an engage under Sivir's ult can win you a game. Sivir's ult is basically an highway : you can either retreat as fast as it's possible, or you can catapult a Nautilus/Shen/Maokai/Kennen in the enemy team. What I find interesting here, it's the fact that she is not OP in herself. You can play it in soloqueue or with friends without stomping anybody easily. It's the current LCS meta that makes her so. To be honest, I don't believe we'll see her in the last week or even in playoff. It's way too dangerous to leave such a threat open.

 

4 - Corki - 5W 4L

Most picked adc, Corki never really fade from the meta. You understand why once you take a look to his kit : lots of poke, mobility, armor shredding, mixed and true damage, and a great powerspike during midgame (the earliest among adc's). Moreover, the fact he deals magic damage makes the itemization pretty hard against a Corki team. I you wanna play a poke team with Varus or Jayce, take Corki ! If you're building an all-in teamfight midgame team, take Corki please ! There isn't much to say about Corki, it's a low-risk high-reward adc and can fill various roles on a team. I won't be surprised to see him as the go-to-carry during playoffs.

 

5 - Rumble - 3W 2L - 4 Bans

Whit this yordle-sized gundam, you want to do two things : either teamfight or siege. In both situations, Rumble excels. Let's take a closer look ! In the first situation you're building a team to win the midgame : you can call it heavy teamfight team, all-in midgame team, etc. the process is the same : you take Rumble, you add some heavy cc and another heavy damage dealer (like Corki or Rek'Sai) and you force the enemy to fight you. You ult, they die, you win. On paper it's straightforward, but we all know the execution of such strat is what makes it risky : if you miss your timing, you will fall behind. In the other hand, Rumble fits so well, once again, in a poke comp ! Rumble - Jayce/Varus - Corki is the fondation of the ultimate poke team. Our robot can either disengage with is ult or, in the best scenario, zone all the enemy team. He's the perfect siege-help tool. Still, he has weaknesses. Meta speaking, you force your support or/and your jungler to play frontlane tanks ; and if he falls behind in early game, it can be an hard backlash.

 

6 - Shen - 3W 4L - 1 Ban

For an unknown reason, Europe doesn't like Nautilus top, but, essentially, Shen plays the same role : a flex pick with a midgame spike that offers lots of things : cc, tankiness and peel. His lack of teamfight utility is balanced by his global presence and his splitpush capacity (if played top, of course). Shen support is an interesting thing as he offers sustain, a powerfull cc and peeling. And yet... I find Nautilus to outperform Shen, either as a support or a toplaner. To quickly end about Shen : he's a polyvalent champ and a flex pick, but he requires a perfect decision making to perform well : a bad teleport or spoiled ult can truly hurt a team. In that regard, Nautilus is a bit more "forgiving". I've the feeling that I haven't yet understood the true impact of Shen, I'll watch with curiosity the next picks of our beloved ninja. (Let's talk about it : in what kind of a world are ninja tanks ?!)

 

Conclusion

In a team building perspective, one can easily understand why these picks are contested and ban-worthy : they may not be the foundation of team compositions but they offer so many great tools to help you build a perfect team. Sure, you can build a poke team without Sivir, Corki or Rumble, but picking them will help you so much.

Next time you see a game, try to ask you these questions : why the coach is prioritizing that champion ? Why is he leaving that strong one open ? What is he trying to build with it ?

 

So, if you have any comment or reflection, please do ! Hoping the read has been interesting !
